steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The gender pay gap: women earn about 8% less per hour (2023). Causes: lower-paid occupations, part-time work, career breaks, glass ceiling. The gap is wider for older women and ethnic minority women.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The glass ceiling: invisible barriers preventing women from reaching top positions. Only 10% of FTSE 100 CEOs are women. The 'glass cliff': women more likely to be appointed during crises.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Gender roles: girls socialised into caring/nurturing, boys into active/independent. Oakley: gender roles are socially constructed. This affects subject choices, career choices, domestic roles.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Feminist perspectives: Liberal (reform through legislation), Marxist (capitalism + patriarchy), Radical (patriarchy is primary oppression), Difference (intersectionality of class, ethnicity, sexuality).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why the gender pay gap exists and evaluate whether legislation can eliminate it. | Compare different Feminist perspectives on gender inequality. | Evaluate whether gender inequality has been significantly reduced in modern Britain.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Gender pay gap = 8%. Causes: occupation, part-time, motherhood penalty, glass ceiling. Glass ceiling = barrier to TOP jobs. Glass cliff = women appointed during CRISIS. Progress YES. Full equality NO. Formal equality exists; substantive equality is incomplete.
